overview.original_building: Headquarters of the Travancore Nair Brigade since 1868; later served as a military hospital

vision: To collect objects of historical and parliamentary significance for display, protection, preservation and research.
To disseminate knowledge about the significance of the objects in respect of history and institutions of democracy.
To serve as a centre for enjoyment and interaction of people in parliamentary and cultural activity.
vision_mission.history: A cultural and architectural landmark in the state of Kerala, the Kerala Legislature Golden Jubilee Museum inspires a passion for democracy and learning. The museum opened at the Kerala Legislative Assembly Complex and is unique — widely acclaimed as a role model for state assemblies elsewhere in the country. The building that housed the museum was the headquarters of the Travancore Nair Brigade since 1868 and later served as a military hospital. It was converted to the Legislative Assembly Museum and inaugurated on 05 May 2006. The museum was expanded with a new building on 15 April 2013.
vision_mission.description: The museum displays photos, objects and artefacts that showcase the rich heritage of democratic institutions of the land. It includes a model assembly hall, mini theatre, library, research centre, multimedia hall and touch-screen kiosks — designed to give every visitor insight into milestones of the Kerala Assembly.

what_museum_offers: The museum is a repository for the rich legislative history of Kerala. Thousands of school students and researchers visit the museum every year as part of education and study tours. Exhibits, multimedia kiosks and a small library make it a practical resource for learning about democratic institutions.

how_to_visit.address: Kerala Legislature Golden Jubilee Museum, Kerala Legislative Assembly Complex, Thiruvananthapuram – 695 001
how_to_visit.by_road: The museum is located inside the Kerala Legislative Assembly Complex, accessible from Vikas Bhavan Road, Thiruvananthapuram.
how_to_visit.by_rail: Nearest railway station: Thiruvananthapuram Central (approx. 3 km)
how_to_visit.by_air: Nearest airport: Trivandrum International Airport (approx. 8 km)
how_to_visit.guided_tours: Available on request for school groups and study tours

what_is_here.title: Model Assembly Hall
what_is_here.description: A scale model of the Kerala Legislative Assembly Hall that gives visitors a realistic view of the chamber where laws are made.

what_is_here.title: Mini Theatre
what_is_here.description: Screens documentary films on the history of the Kerala Legislature and democratic institutions of the state.

what_is_here.title: Multimedia Hall
what_is_here.description: Interactive multimedia presentations on the evolution of democracy in Kerala from ancient times to the present.

what_is_here.title: Touch-screen Kiosks
what_is_here.description: Self-guided interactive kiosks that allow visitors to explore milestones of the Kerala Assembly at their own pace.

what_is_here.title: Research Centre
what_is_here.description: A dedicated space for researchers and scholars to access archival materials and historical documents related to the Kerala Legislature.

what_is_here.title: Historical Photos & Artefacts
what_is_here.description: A curated collection of photographs, objects and artefacts that showcase the rich heritage of democratic institutions of Kerala.

what_is_here.title: Sales Division
what_is_here.description: Offers publications, souvenirs and educational materials related to the Kerala Legislature and its history.

what_is_here.title: Children's Library
what_is_here.description: A dedicated library section for young visitors with books and resources on democracy, history and Kerala's legislative heritage.
